page: Microsoft Azure PB6s is an x86_64 virtual machine instance belonging to the PBS family running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile is equipped with 6 dedicated Intel vCPUs and 112.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 18.67 GB of RAM per virtual processor. Local storage consists of a 790 GB SSD, and the configuration supports Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not feature discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The architecture emphasizes memory capacity over compute core density. With over 18 GB of memory per core, the server accommodates data sets that exceed standard general-purpose thresholds without requiring allocation of higher vCPU counts. The inclusion of 790 GB of direct local solid-state storage allows temporary file handling and local caching without incurring separate network storage latency. No hardware acceleration from GPUs is present, and advanced vector or cryptographic instruction extensions are not exposed in the CPU flags.

Qualitatively, the resource distribution targets workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than parallel CPU execution. Microsoft Azure PB6s fits operational profiles such as in-memory databases, caching systems, batch ETL pipelines, and specialized analytics tasks where high memory capacity and local SSD throughput are required.

With its elevated memory-to-core ratio, the system offers high memory density without requiring excessive virtual CPU overhead. The server is well suited for memory-intensive operational workloads, including in-memory data processing, caching clusters, relational database hosting, and memory-heavy analytics.
